    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.invertedOn_end_action {R : Type u} [Ring R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : ModuleCat R) (h : P.InvertedOn M) :
    have ρ := Module.toModuleEnd ℤ ↑M; P.InvertedOn ↧(Module.End ℤ ↑M)

    Solving the inversion equations pointwise gives a solution with values in the additive endomorphisms. Uniqueness makes each solution additive.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.finite_stableInvertingClasses_of_finite_localization {R B : Type u} [Ring R] [Ring B] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite k B] (P : TwoTerm R) (g : R →ₐ[k] B) (h : IsUniversalLocalization (fun (x : Unit) => P) g.toRingHom) :

      Over a finite-dimensional localization every stable inverting module is the restriction of a simple module. In particular there are only finitely many stable isomorphism classes on a single inversion chart.
